subject: ss-haematology
title: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas: high-yield essentials

steps.tx: Key subtypes are linked to a **signature translocation**. Follicular lymphoma carries t(14;18) with BCL2 overexpression in over 85 percent of cases. Mantle cell lymphoma shows t(11;14) with cyclin D1. Burkitt lymphoma shows MYC rearrangement, usually t(8;14), with Ki-67 near 100 percent.
steps.say: Each major subtype has a signature translocation. Follicular lymphoma carries t(14;18), which drives BCL2 overexpression, and this is found in over eighty-five percent of cases. Mantle cell lymphoma shows t(11;14) with cyclin D1. Burkitt lymphoma shows a MYC rearrangement, usually t(8;14), with a Ki-67 index near one hundred percent.

steps.tx: Treatment of **diffuse large B-cell lymphoma** (DLBCL) aims at cure in most fit patients. The standard **R-CHOP** regimen pairs **rituximab**, an anti-CD20 antibody, with multi-agent chemotherapy: cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and vincristine, plus a corticosteroid. The **International Prognostic Index** (IPI) estimates risk using age, LDH, performance status, stage and extranodal involvement, guiding how intensively patients are treated.
steps.say: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is usually treated with curative intent. The standard R-CHOP regimen combines rituximab, an antibody against CD20, with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and vincristine, plus a corticosteroid. The International Prognostic Index estimates risk from age, lactate dehydrogenase, performance status, stage and extranodal disease, helping clinicians decide how intensive treatment should be.

steps.tx: **Burkitt lymphoma** is a haematological emergency because its very rapid cell turnover carries a high risk of **tumour lysis syndrome**. Management starts before chemotherapy, with aggressive intravenous hydration, uric acid lowering therapy and close electrolyte monitoring. Treatment then proceeds to an intensive, short-duration **chemoimmunotherapy** course with **CNS-directed prophylaxis**, because the disease frequently involves the central nervous system.
steps.say: Burkitt lymphoma is a haematological emergency because its rapid cell turnover carries a high risk of tumour lysis syndrome. Treatment begins with intravenous hydration, uric acid lowering therapy and close electrolyte monitoring. It then moves to an intensive, short-duration chemoimmunotherapy course with central nervous system directed prophylaxis, since this lymphoma often involves the brain and spinal fluid spaces.

nodes.label: Hydration, uric acid lowering and electrolyte monitoring

steps.tx: Double-hit lymphoma carries **MYC** plus **BCL2** or **BCL6** rearrangement and is classed as a separate high-grade entity, not simply Burkitt lymphoma. Relapsed **mantle cell lymphoma** after chemoimmunotherapy and **BTK inhibitor** failure may be offered **CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy**. Gastric **MALT lymphoma** carrying **t(11;18)** tends to respond poorly to H. pylori eradication, so alternative treatment is usually needed.
